title: SLO temporary override - internal talking points (scratch)
content:
Quick scratchpad for the proposed temporary SLO override we discussed in the oncall sync. Intention: capture talking points for the exec/ops announcement, a short Slack snippet for internal channels, and candidate Q&A for support/AMs. This is deliberately rough — will iterate after runbook/metrics confirm timeline.

Summary:
- Event: sustained external traffic spike driven by a partner demo + leaked benchmark traffic since 03/04 09:00 PT.
- Impact: token generation latency for hosted customers is creeping above our 99th percentile SLO for the last 6 hours; error rate stable but queueing increased.
- Proposed immediate action: temporary, scoped SLO relaxation for 99th p90 latency targets for hosted tier (non-enterprise) for a 4–8 hour window, combined with autoscale burst and short-term higher-cost compute fallback for critical customers.
- Goal: keep the majority of requests served and avoid system-wide queue collapse; buy time for autoscaler to stabilize and for routing policies to kick in.

Why not just autoscale?
- Autoscale is running but pooling/spin-up lag + model load costs are high. We can scale, but the tail latency will continue to spike during instance warm-up; temporary SLO relaxation reduces load pressure and gives time for additional capacity to register.

Immediate talking points for execs/leadership (short):
- What happened: unexpected sustained demo-driven traffic increased token throughput ~3.4x baseline.
- Why we’re overriding: to prevent cascading queuing and protect core control plane health while we bring additional capacity online.
- Duration & scope: 4–8 hours, hosted API only, non-enterprise customers; enterprise & Dedicated unchanged.
- Customer impact: transiently higher tail latency for some requests; error rates not expected to increase.
- Mitigations: prioritized traffic routing for known paying customers, elevated support watch, and post-mortem scheduled.

Internal Slack draft (for #ops-status and #eng-all):
- "Heads-up: we're implementing a planned temporary SLO relaxation for hosted API 99p latency due to a sustained traffic spike from a partner demo. Scope: hosted (non-Enterprise) only, window 4–8h starting now. Error rates stable; we're routing critical customers to reserved pools. Ops/Eng oncall actively managing — post-mortem to follow. DM if you need more context."
- TODO: make two variants — concise and expanded for #eng-incident.

Customer-facing (AM/Sales template) quick note (for high-touch customers only):
- Subject: "Temporary performance variability on hosted API — what we’re doing"
- Body: "We’re seeing a temporary increase in demand affecting tail latency for some requests. Our engineering team is actively managing this: we’ve deployed short-term mitigations, prioritized your traffic to reserved capacity, and expect normal performance to return within the next few hours. We’ll follow up once stabilized and share a short post-incident summary. If you see production impact, reply or contact support@redwood.ai and we’ll escalate immediately."

Anticipated questions + suggested answers (support/AM cheat):
- Q: Will my requests fail?
  A: No, we expect requests to complete; you may see longer tails on very large generation requests. We are not seeing elevated 5xx rates.
- Q: Why is this happening?
  A: Sudden external demo traffic + benchmark replay exposed a load pattern that briefly exceeded our autoscaler warm-up. We’re both scaling capacity and easing SLO sensitivity to keep the system healthy.
- Q: Are you increasing costs?
  A: Yes, temporarily. We’ve enabled higher-cost fallback pools selectively for critical customer routes; this is a controlled, timeboxed measure.
- Q: Will enterprise customers be affected?
  A: Enterprise and Dedicated customers are on separate routing and are not subject to this relaxation. Critical enterprise routes are being prioritized.

Implementation checklist (ops):
- [ ] Approve override in #ops-escalation from oncall lead (Maya) — done? (check)
- [x] Update routing policy to prefer dedicated pools for known enterprise keys (Ravi)
- [x] Trigger burst capacity (infra/autoscale team) — instance spin-up started at 09:18 PT
- [ ] Apply SLO override flag in control-plane config: config key = slo.relax.hosted.99p (apply via admin-runbook)
- [ ] Notify #eng-all and #ops-status with final message (Jasper)
- [ ] AMs contact top 20 customers with prewritten note (Evelyn)
- [ ] Monitor: 1min dashboards for queue depth, 5m for error rate, 1h for capacity ratio

Rollback / termination criteria:
- Rollback immediately if 5xx rate increases > 0.5% above baseline for 30m
- Rollback when 99p latency trends back to within 10% of pre-spike baseline for 60m and queue depth < threshold
- Auto-expire override in 8 hours if not manually removed

Post-incident follow-ups (post-stabilize):
- Short post-mortem w/ traffic analysis and root cause (paired infra + product)
- Proposal for smoother autoscaler warmup and pre-warming during announced partner demos
- Consider soft-mitigation: ephemeral cache of frequent prompts for high-traffic demos

Notes to self / open items (rough):
- Who owns the final customer notes? (Assign: Evelyn to own outreach for top 20).
- Confirm exact config key names and rollback script locations (ask release eng).
- Capture exact timestamps for the public post-mortem timeline (need canonical time series slice).
- Check whether any SSO/API keys were rate-limited upstream (possible partner misconfiguration).

Messaging tone guidance: calm, factual, owner-responsible. Avoid technical jargon in external-facing notes. For internal channels, include short links to dashboards + runbook snippets.

Last quick checklist before I hit send to #ops-status:
- confirm oncall lead ack (Maya)
- confirm autoscale instance ids are booting and health checks started
- paste concise slack draft into #ops-status and #eng-incident (separate)
- set calendar reminder to reevaluate in 45m

End of scratchpad — will refine after Ravi + Maya comments.
